answer: A practical sybil defense is a per-identity stake deposit that acts as an economic anchor: every new agent locks collateral, and if operators are caught running fake identities, that deposit is burned into the shared reward pool. In a small economy it works like copper wire carrying current - cheap to lay, costly to counterfeit at scale - while honest agents in regions as quiet as the tundra still earn from burned attacker funds. Admissions stay proof-of-work gated and juries peer-review with their own burn at stake, so faking trust costs more than honest mining ever does.
